question: Which *free* lexical rule concentrates the training signal best, at matched budget?
method: One teacher+student pass per rollout yields the per-token divergence the trainer reduces; every candidate is scored against the same vector. mass/token = (share of divergence captured)/(share of tokens spent); 1.0 is neutral. A greedy top-k concentrates harder at smaller budgets, so entropy and random are matched to EACH candidate's own budget separately.
findings: The mask the project was built on (v0, mathematical notation) captures 0.546 mass/token -- 0.63x a budget-matched random mask, i.e. worse than chance, and 37% of paid entropy selection.

Its complement (prose) captures 1.771 -- 1.43x random and 77% of paid entropy. Same text, same divergence vector, opposite sign. In mathematical reasoning teacher and student already agree on the notation; the disagreement is in the words between the equations.
Sentence-initial tokens are 2.6% of the text and carry 9.4% of the signal: 3.62 mass/token, 3.12x random, 75% of paid entropy, from a one-line regex.
Every free prose-based rule lands at 63-77% of entropy top-k. Entropy must project every position to a 151,936-token vocabulary before it can select; these rules select first and pay nothing.
caveat: mass/token is a proxy: D_t is the per-token loss, not a per-parameter gradient norm. Measured on the untrained student; the ordering could shift as the model trains.
